 UFC Fight Night: Shamil Gaziev vs Tallison Teixeira Preview & Prediction
 by Owen Liao · 20 November 2026 at 12:11 pm 
 Updated 20 November 2026 at 12:46 pm 
 Post 
 Share 
 Click here for today’s sports betting tips from our expert analysts! 
 Two heavy hitters crash on the prelims, Bahrain’s Shamil Gaziev takes on the towering Brazilian Tallison Teixeira in a heavyweight fight unlikely to trouble the judges.

 Shamil Gaziev: Front loaded power with a fading gas tank
 Shamil Gaziev (15-3) bounced back in August with a first round TKO of Kennedy Nzechukwu after back-to-back knockout losses. Those came against two difficult opponents in the ranked Waldo Cortes-Acosta and the pressure-heavy Brando Pericic. His only other loss was a fourth round stoppage against Jairzinho Rozenstruik, when his weak cardio caught up with him. When he’s confident, Gaziev marches forward behind heavy straight shots and rarely kicks. He’s very physical in the clinch, with body lock takedowns and ground and pound, but he’s fairly hittable and his power drops off steeply as the rounds go on.
 Tallison Teixeira: Towering Muay Thai threat with chinny concerns
 Tallison Teixeira (9-2) is a towering heavyweight with a massive frame, standing 6'7" with an 83-inch reach. He fights long in a Muay Thai style, with straight punches and high kicks, and meets opponents halfway with elbows when they close the distance. All of his knockouts have come in the opening round, but his weakness is boxing in the pocket. Derrick Lewis and Sergei Pavlovich both closed that reach gap and stopped him inside a minute, the Pavlovich loss coming in May. He fights very upright and leaves his chin open in exchanges.
 Shamil Gaziev vs Tallison Teixeira prediction
 I think this is Gaziev’s fight all day. Teixeira has the range advantage, but we’ve seen what happens when someone walks through that reach and makes him box in the pocket, and that’s exactly where Gaziev wants to be. Both fighters are fairly hittable when trading, and when they meet in the middle, I think Gaziev’s power outmatches Teixeira’s. He should also have the better durability to survive the slugfest, given Teixeira has been stopped inside a minute twice.
 Gaziev has the better wins on record too, and his first-round stoppage of Thomas Petersen is fairly underrated. Petersen has since beaten and fraud checked two prospects in Guilherme Pat and Gabriel Lorenco, weathering the early storm against both power punchers before taking over. Gaziev didn’t give him the chance to do that, and that’s an impressive look in hindsight.
 Neither man’s power holds up deep into a fight, so this will be a power punching showcase. Don’t expect to see the judges’ scorecards, and don’t expect much technical to break down. It’ll be wild while it lasts, and I think Gaziev lands the bigger shot early.
 Prediction: Shamil Gaziev to win by KO/TKO in round one
